paragraphs: A field-by-field tour of the Caspio REST v4 surface, pulled from the account's live Swagger. v4 is a superset of v3, opt-in, and additive — our existing v3 integrations (the whole caspio-pricing-proxy) keep working untouched. Everything here is what is new or changed relative to v3.

v4 adds bulk operations with safety rails, full T-SQL in query parameters, single-call schema discovery, first-class file/webhook/app endpoints, and a machine-readable "AI context" so agents can drive the API. Our proxy still runs v3 — adopt v4 per-endpoint only where a new power pays off.

The v4 launch shipped as part of Caspio 73.0. Several 73.0 changes are platform-level and matter beyond the endpoint list — some affect our existing v2/v3 integrations. Full notes: howto.caspio.com/release-notes/caspio-73-0.

REST endpoints now return 403 Forbidden when the calling API profile lacks object-level permission (Data Import/Export Tasks, Bridge Apps); Tables password-field & attachment reads now return 404 for missing objects. Action: confirm our proxy's API profile has "Enable access to all objects" ON (Integrations → API Profiles) so the ~397 proxy calls don't silently start 403-ing, and treat a 403 as an auth-scope error (surface it — never swallow).

Each outgoing webhook now carries an HMAC-SHA256 signature (secret = the webhook's autogenerated secret / regenerateSecret) so a receiver can prove it came from Caspio, unmodified. Compatibility mode for receivers that can't compute an HMAC: include the secret in the payload (defaultPayloadIncludesSecret / [@out-hook:secret]). Capture the exact signature header from the authenticated v4 Swagger when we build the receiver.

If any receiver or firewall allowlists Caspio's egress IPs, add the new ones (all /32 IPv4, US set): 3.94.26.149, 3.221.12.171, 3.223.237.156, 3.232.188.127, 18.235.29.217, 34.200.156.163, 35.173.3.24, 44.198.154.72, 44.219.25.193, 44.221.229.56, 54.88.136.246, 54.224.65.145, 100.58.20.55. The list may change without notice. (NWCA's 24 webhooks target Zapier today, so no NWCA-owned allowlist is affected yet.)

Redesigned API Profile Management (Integrations → API Profiles) — granular default permissions by object type + per-object overrides, generate a bearer token from the UI and test in the built-in Swagger UI, and IPv6 + IP-range access control. This is the path to split our single-credential blast radius into scoped least-privilege profiles.
Flex — Theme Editor (per-Segment themes, live preview, reusable) + Date/Time minute-level min/max offsets and fixed daily time windows.
Vault — create app packages directly from a Flex application's menu.
v4 is self-describing — a client or AI agent can bootstrap without hard-coding anything.
Request a task-scoped subset instead of the full 63-path spec (keeps agents inside token/operation limits):
All data endpoints require Authorization: Bearer {access_token}. Auth is identical to v3 — same token endpoint and lifecycle.

POST {tokenEndpoint} # account subdomain, same host family as the API base Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded grant_type=client_credentials&client_id={clientId}&client_secret={clientSecret} → { "access_token":"…", "token_type":"bearer", "expires_in":86399, "refresh_token":"…" }
Cache & reuse access_token; renew after expires_in (~24h). Refresh without re-sending creds: grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token={…}.

Each API profile has an isolated permission boundary scoped to specific tables/views — an application-level allowlist enforced before any SQL runs. Out-of-grant references are rejected as IncorrectQueryParameter.
Our implementation: caspio-pricing-proxy/src/utils/caspio.js → getCaspioAccessToken() (module-cached, 60s buffer). 400 "IncorrectQueryParameter" = stale token, auto-retried once per page.
Query parameters are plain camelCase (no q. prefix):
Always reference a field by its Name, never its Label.
Strings need the Unicode prefix in where: N'value'. Escape single quotes by doubling: N'O''Brien'.
YES/NO fields: use 1/0 in where, but send JSON true/false in write payloads.
Cross-table subqueries are permitted & encouraged; the permission boundary still applies. System catalogs are blocked and DDL (CREATE/ALTER/DROP) is never allowed.
Rich SQL-driven analytics straight through REST — no stored procedures, middleware, or pre-built Caspio views. Reporting aggregation (e.g. daily-sales-by-rep) could move server-side.
List endpoints return an envelope — read records from data[], use pagination.totalCount to compute pages:
{ "data": [ … ], "pagination": { "totalCount": N, "pageNumber": N, "pageSize": N } }
Every write endpoint accepts an optional echo=true query parameter to return the affected record(s).

Bulk insert takes a JSON array (max 1000) and returns 201 when all succeed or 207 Multi-Status on partial failure — the response is a Result[] array where each element carries a per-item Status (201=created, 4xx/5xx=failure):
POST /v4/tables/{tableId}/records/bulk [ { "FieldA": 1 }, { "FieldA": 2 } ] → { "Result": [ { "Status":201, "PK_ID":"101" }, { "Status":422, "error":"…" } ] }

Note the envelopes differ: list endpoints return data[] + pagination, but bulk insert returns Result[] with a capital-S Status per item (confirmed against the live spec). Verify exact casing before writing a parser.
Conditional bulk update & delete require a where:
BulkUpdateRecordsRequest — where * (required) + recordValues * (required)
BulkDeleteRecordsRequest — where * (required)

An always-true filter (1=1, PK_ID>0) would hit every row — irreversible for DELETE. When the server's tautology guard is active, such unscoped filters are rejected. Always target with something like PK_ID IN (1,2,3) or Status=N'Inactive', and run a SELECT with the same where first to confirm the row count.
{ "Code":"ERROR_CODE", "Message":"human description", "Resource":"/path", "RequestId":"…", "DocumentationUrl":"…", "Hint": { "Note":"…", "Remediation":"…" } }

Every error links back to /v4/errors/{code} for a machine-readable hint + remediation. Structural deletes (deleting a table, folder, or Flex app) return 405 by design as schema protection — not a missing feature.
Fields flagged Editable=false are auto-generated and must never appear in POST/PUT/PATCH bodies.

POST/PATCH …/fields use FieldModelV4 (name*, dataType*, label, displayOrder, unique, isFormula, format, prefix, length, listField[], stampOnInsert/Update+stampTimeZone, attachment controls). Reads return richer FieldItemV4 (+editable, formula, relationship).

One call, everything: GET /v4/schemas/tables (also /views, /directories, /outgoingWebhooks) returns every accessible object with full field definitions, relationships, and triggered actions. Ideal when object names are unknown — kills field-list hard-coding.

Relationships are explicit (TableRelationshipItem: relationshipType, joinType, parent/child table+field, referentialIntegrity, cascadeUpdate/Delete, displayValue) — see joins without reverse-engineering views.
List / search files & folders, upload (POST new, PUT overwrite), download or delete by fileId (GUID) or by path.
Metadata: fileId, name, size, contentType, fullFilePath. New-file upload returns 409 Conflict if the name already exists.
Typical FILE-field flow: stored path → GET /v4/fileAssets/files/path/fileInfo (resolve the fileId) → GET …/files/{fileId} (download).
Download / upload-replace (PUT) / delete a single attachment by record + field name.
Bulk attachment ops by condition: upload to many records, get/rename file metadata, delete matching files.
Full CRUD for outgoing webhooks and their events, plus PATCH …/{webhookId}/regenerateSecret. Events use WebhookEventV4PostRequest:

WebhookEventV4PostRequest { type * string // required objectId * string // required — the table/directory objectFields string[] eventSources string[] defaultPayloadIncludesSecret boolean defaultPayloadFields string[] customPayloadTemplate string enabled boolean }
Triggered-action rules surface (read-only) through schema discovery as TriggeredActionItem (name, eventType, isEnabled, referencedObjects[] + audit stamps).

Caspio Outgoing Webhooks FIRE on REST writes (≠ Triggered Actions, which do NOT fire on REST). v4 gives full webhook CRUD — reinforces the roadmap to convert polling crons → authenticated push. Guard against feedback loops (scope eventSources/objectFields, idempotent dedupe).
Flex applications — list & read (AppItemV4: appId, name, dataPageCount, icon, audit stamps).
Bridge applications — list/read apps, list their DataPages, read a DataPage, get its deployment code, and deploy/undeploy one or (in bulk) all DataPages.
Data Import/Export tasks — list, read, and POST …/{taskId}/run. ScheduledTaskInfoV4 exposes status, recurrence, last-run time/result, and time zone.

Current state: caspio-pricing-proxy calls Caspio v3 exclusively. The single migration chokepoint is caspio-pricing-proxy/src/utils/caspio.js (token cache, fetchAllCaspioPages(), base URL https://c3eku948.caspio.com/integrations/rest/v3).
Bulk conditional writes instead of per-record loops (respect the tautology guard; SELECT-first).
Single-call schema discovery to stop hard-coding field lists.
T-SQL where/select for analytics without pre-built Caspio views.
Outgoing-webhook CRUD to replace polling crons (webhook-fires-on-REST).
/v4/aiManifest + lenses for AI-driven tooling.

Drop the q. prefix → read from data[] not Result[] → use pageNumber+pageSize → N'…' string literals + 1/0 in where (but true/false in bodies) → confirm the token's profile grants the referenced objects. v3 works today; migrate an endpoint only when a specific v4 power justifies it.

Generated from the live Caspio REST API v4 Swagger definition at /integrations/rest/v4/swagger/documentation (OpenAPI 3.0.4). Existing v3 integrations are unaffected — v4 is additive and adopted on our own schedule. Canonical memory copy: memory/CASPIO_REST_API_V4_REFERENCE.md. Docs: howto.caspio.com (how-to) · authenticated Swagger UI (live tables/apps + full v4 schemas).

Field reference for the ShopWorks OnSite External API ("ManageOrders") — the API we push orders to and pull order/tracking data from. Every field of the order-push structure, annotated with the gotchas we've learned in production.
Dates are MM/DD/YYYY on push (the Swagger says ISO — OnSite rejects ISO).

TaxTotal: 0 — OnSite drops the order-level tax on import. Put tax in a Notes block; the rep applies it via the ShopWorks dropdown. Tax flags sts_EnableTax01–04 (undocumented in Swagger) drive tax calc if used.
Color = CATALOG_COLOR (mainframe code), never COLOR_NAME. id_Design: omit (don't send 0) when unknown. Size: push the BASE part# + plain size — OnSite appends _2X/_3X.
Only 4 valid Notes[].Type values — one bad Type aborts the WHOLE push. ExtOrderID/ExtDesignID must be GLOBALLY unique (full date+seq+year).
GET /order-pull returns fields at the TOP level (Swagger shows them wrapped in order_json — it's wrong). Retention ≈ 2 years, not 60 days.
Full detail (165+ fields, per-endpoint examples, tested behavior) → the canonical memory/MANAGEORDERS_COMPLETE_REFERENCE.md. This page is the quick lookup.

Compiled from the two public Swaggers — push ShopWorks/OnSiteExternalAPI/1.0.0 (host /onsite) + pull ShopWorks/ManageOrdersAPI/1.0.0 (host /v1) — plus tested behavior in memory/MANAGEORDERS_COMPLETE_REFERENCE.md (the single source of truth — update THERE, not here). Push chokepoint: caspio-pricing-proxy/lib/manageorders-push-client.js.

Field + method reference for the SanMar Web Services API — the XML/SOAP services we use for product data, live inventory, pricing, order status/shipments, invoices, and packing slips (Box Labels). From the Integration Guide v24.5 (July 2026), annotated with our production gotchas.

Color = catalogColor / mainframe code ("BrillOrng"), never the display COLOR_NAME — for every SanMar API, inventory, and order call. (One exception: our proxy's /api/inventory product feed keys on COLOR_NAME.)
Inventory caps at 3000/warehouse — a returned "3000" means ≥3000, not an exact count (both inventory services).
sizeIndex is a small ordinal (1=XS, 2=S, 3=M, 4=L, 5=XL, 6+=2XL…). uniqueKey = inventoryKey+sizeIndex = PromoStandards partId — the CSV merge key.
Use PRODUCTION WSDLs even for read testing — the Test env's products/pricing/inventory are stale. Test credentials are separate.

Order tracking: error 301 = order not shipped+invoiced yet (persisting >48h → flag + pause); 303 = date older than 7 days; allOpen excludes Complete — a fast order can vanish between polls (pair with invoice-based catch-up).
Standard getPricing = cost tiers, not MSRP, and price varies by color. MSRP/MAP = PromoStandards priceType=List or the mapPrice field (new Jun 2026).

Product Data V2 also answers at …/ProductDataServiceV2.xml?wsdl — prefer the Binding form (what our proxy uses). Order Status V1 was removed Aug 2024 — never re-add it. API IP 63.251.12.134; a WSDL timeout in a browser = port-8080 firewall block.
Standard: Invalid Style + Color + Size specified (use SanMar_SDL_N.csv for valid combos) · User authentication failed · Invalid warehouse specified.

PromoStandards codes: 100 ID not found · 104 unauthorized · 105 auth failed · 110 auth required · 115 wsVersion · 120 required fields · 125 not supported · 130 productId · 135 product color · 140 partId · 145 part color · 150 part size · 155 date format · 160 no results · 200 product data not found · 300 queryType · 301 PO/invoice not found (must be shipped + invoiced) · 302 bad timestamp · 303 date >7 days old · 999 general.

Prohibited on Amazon/eBay/Etsy/Craigslist/any third-party or D2C site (14): Brooks Brothers · Carhartt · Cotopaxi · Eddie Bauer · MiiR Apparel (new) · New Era · Nike · OGIO · Outdoor Research · Stanley/Stella · tentree · The North Face · Tommy Bahama · Travis Mathew.
Hemmed pants: NOT in integrated data or PO submittal — order via SanMar.com/phone/email (unhemmed = supported). GTINs for most brands: SanMar_SDL_N.csv / SanMar_EPDD.csv.

Compiled from the SanMar Web Services Integration Guide v24.5 (July 2026) — PDF: memory/sanmar-api-guide-24.5-jul2026.pdf — plus tested behavior in memory/SANMAR_API_REFERENCE.md (the single source of truth — update THERE, not here). PO submission (outbound blank ordering) is separate → memory/sanmar-po/README.md. Onboarding/access: sanmarintegrations@sanmar.com.

Read-only SQL access to the OnSite FileMaker database via the FileMaker ODBC (xDBC) driver — the data layer underneath the ManageOrders API. 17 tables, 2,630 fields, including due dates, customer credit/terms, job costing, commissions, and the production-floor log that ManageOrders can't return. Verified live 2026-07-16.
Never blanket-query. Always filter (WHERE on a stored, indexed field) + FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY. Unbounded scans can fill the server's C: drive and crash OnSite for everyone.
Never poll tightly. Automated queries run minutes apart, not seconds. One connection, sequential queries — the xDBC listener serializes work.
DSN points at Data_ODBCMapping only. Never other files, never modify it, never create extra DSNs.
Resetting the ODBC connector (FileMaker Server Admin Console) disconnects ALL ODBC clients — including the shipping machines. Coordinate before touching it; shipping software must be restarted after.
No images/attachments via ODBC (design thumbnails, PDFs). No writes ever — the extro account is read-only; order creation stays on the ManageOrders push API.

Need a table/field that isn't mapped? Full-screen OnSite screenshots with fields highlighted → support@shopworx.com. They annotate table/field names and extend the mapping. (Known unmapped: LinesPur — PO line items.)

The FileMaker driver and the querying app must live on the same Windows machine — bandit fills that role (always-on; already had both drivers from the shipping integration). Remote-query pattern from an authorized laptop:

$cred = Import-Clixml "$env:USERPROFILE\bandit-cred.xml" Invoke-Command -ComputerName bandit -Credential $cred -ScriptBlock { $c = New-Object System.Data.Odbc.OdbcConnection ` 'DRIVER={FileMaker ODBC};Server=192.168.10.6;Database=Data_ODBCMapping;UID=extro;PWD=extro' $c.Open() # ... bounded SELECT here ... $c.Close() }

Production plan (not yet built): scheduled sync agent on bandit → proxy bulk-upsert route → Caspio tables + freshness watchdog. Heroku can never reach the DSN directly (no Linux driver; LAN-only address). Canonical doc: memory/SHOPWORKS_ODBC_INTEGRATION.md.
The laptop is a workgroup machine and bandit is on the NWEINC domain, so PowerShell Remoting needs two one-time steps (no Kerberos between them). Repeat these on any new/replacement laptop:

Trust bandit — in an Administrator PowerShell (Start → type powershell → "Run as Administrator"): Set-Service WinRM -StartupType Manual Start-Service WinRM Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Client\TrustedHosts -Value 'bandit,bandit.NWEINC.local,192.168.10.219' -Force Get-Item WSMan:\localhost\Client\TrustedHosts # verify the 3 entries Trusts bandit specifically (no wildcard). If Set-Item says "cannot connect to the destination", the local WinRM service isn't running — the first two lines fix that. "Access is denied" = window isn't elevated.

Set-Service WinRM -StartupType Manual Start-Service WinRM Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Client\TrustedHosts -Value 'bandit,bandit.NWEINC.local,192.168.10.219' -Force Get-Item WSMan:\localhost\Client\TrustedHosts # verify the 3 entries

Store the bandit login — in a normal (non-admin) PowerShell, so the file is encrypted under your everyday account: Get-Credential NWEINC\Erik | Export-Clixml "$env:USERPROFILE\bandit-cred.xml" Enter the password you use to log into bandit. The file is DPAPI-encrypted — readable only by this Windows user on this machine; the password never appears in scripts or chat. ⚠ Re-run this step after any bandit/domain password change — the stored credential goes stale and remoting starts failing with auth errors.
Get-Credential NWEINC\Erik | Export-Clixml "$env:USERPROFILE\bandit-cred.xml"

Use it — any PowerShell session (or Claude in chat) can now run queries ON bandit: $cred = Import-Clixml "$env:USERPROFILE\bandit-cred.xml" Invoke-Command -ComputerName bandit -Credential $cred -ScriptBlock { hostname } # smoke test → BANDIT
$cred = Import-Clixml "$env:USERPROFILE\bandit-cred.xml" Invoke-Command -ComputerName bandit -Credential $cred -ScriptBlock { hostname } # smoke test → BANDIT
"WinRM cannot process the request / TrustedHosts" → step 1 wasn't done (or a new laptop). Re-run it.
Auth/logon failure on Invoke-Command → stale credential file after a password change → re-run step 2.
Times out / host unreachable → laptop is off the shop LAN (192.168.10.x) — this only works on-site (or via VPN), or bandit is off/asleep (ping 192.168.10.219, RDP is also open as a fallback).
ODBC errors IM002/IM014 on bandit → app/driver bitness mismatch — bandit has BOTH drivers; 64-bit PowerShell/Python uses the 64-bit driver + the SWODBC System DSN, 32-bit apps use SW32/SWAddress.
Connection opens but queries hang → the fmxdbc_listener on the OnSite server may be wedged — resetting it in FMS Admin Console kicks off the shipping machines too; coordinate first.
Row limits: FETCH FIRST 100 ROWS ONLY (no LIMIT/TOP). Paging: OFFSET n ROWS before it — but prefer delta-sync on date_Modification.
Dates: {d '2026-07-16'} / {ts '2026-07-16 14:00:00'}. Never BETWEEN on dates — pathologically slow; use >= AND <=.
Empty string = NULL. col = '' matches nothing → use IS NULL / IS NOT NULL.
Case-sensitive strings. 'a' <> 'A'. LOWER() works but kills index use.
Booleans are 1/0 — no TRUE/FALSE keywords.
Joins: INNER + LEFT OUTER only (no RIGHT/FULL — rewrite as LEFT).

⚠ THE BIG ONE — calc fields: prefixes cn_ ct_ cd_ cm_ co_ cnCur_ cnPer_ sum_ are unstored calculations/summaries — evaluated per-row, unindexable. Never in WHERE; avoid in SELECT. One calc field can turn a sub-second query into minutes of server CPU. gn_ gt_ gd_ gm_ go_ = globals (session values — useless to us). Plain date_ cur_ sts_ ID_ id_ fields are stored → fast.
Never SELECT * — explicit column lists only (wide tables evaluate every calc per row).
Schema discovery: SELECT TableName, FieldName, FieldType FROM FileMaker_Fields (.NET GetSchemaTable() overflows on wide tables — FM15 driver bug).
Repeating fields (decimal[14], varchar[10]) need special handling — plain SELECT returns repetition 1.
Expect dropped connections. The fmxdbc_listener process can wedge; set timeouts, retry once, then alert.
Multi-state status codes: sts_* = 0 No · 1 Yes · .5 Partial · 8/222 N/A (same as ManageOrders).
ODBC does not do: images/attachments · writes (ManageOrders push stays the only write path) · webhooks (still pull-based).
